pages.title: Tidepool Timekeepers Lab Display Clock
pages.notebookSkill: Turning timed observations into story order
pages.visitFit: Adult-led museum or gallery table page for a calm exhibit-clue stop, color noticing, and a short fiction note.
pages.adultSetup: Print one page per writer, choose a quiet display corner, and point out one label, one pattern, and one object shape before writing.
pages.kidDirection: Notice a tidepool exhibit clue, add time-order details, and turn the display into a tiny lab story note.
pages.guidePrompt: Ask the writer what changed first, what changed next, and which label clue belongs in the story.

pageSections.heading: Exhibit Clock
lines: The tidepool exhibit clue shows a time near ____________________.
The display color that changes first is ____________________.
The object shape I notice on the label is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Observation Order
lines: First, the lab helper records ____________________.
Next, the tide pattern points toward ____________________.
Last, the quiet sketch should show ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Fiction Note
lines: The timekeeper's notebook begins with ____________________.
The exhibit clue becomes important because ____________________.
My final tidepool story note says ____________________.

pages.shareLine: The time-order detail I can share from this page is ____________________.
pages.wrapUpLine: One museum observation I turned into fiction was ____________________.
pages.quietOptionLine: For a quiet option, sketch the tide pattern first and label ____________________.
pages.takeHomePromptLine: Take-home prompt: Find a safe household object shape and imagine its exhibit clue: ____________________.

pages.title: Greenhouse Gear Garden Label Design
pages.notebookSkill: Explaining how a display detail changes a made-up machine

pages.adultSetup: Print the page, set pencils beside the viewing spot, and invite writers to compare one gear shape, one plant color, and one short label.
pages.kidDirection: Choose a greenhouse gear from the display, describe what it helps, and write how it changes the garden story.
pages.guidePrompt: Ask which exhibit clue shows the gear's job and which pattern proves the garden needs a small adjustment.

pages.kidDirection: Study the pantry-style exhibit clue, compare the measurement pattern, and write the reason behind the mystery.

pages.kidDirection: Follow the rain-gauge exhibit clue, choose map words, and write the railway route as a story note.
